title: Choose Life
subtitle: Deuteronomy in Poems & Pictures
beforeYouBegin:
Deuteronomy is Moses' farewell. The people are camped on the plains of Moab, with the wilderness behind them and the Jordan in front, and an old man stands up to remind them of everything: sandals that did not wear out in forty years, bread that came with the dew, a God who carried them like a father carries a child. He tells them to write his words on their doorposts, to open their hands to the poor, to leave a sheaf in the field for the widow, and to choose life. Then he climbs a mountain, sees the land, and is buried in a valley no one can find.

This book walks through it in thirty-six short poems, in four parts. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the book of Deuteronomy alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: Part One · Remember the Road
parts.epigraph: You shall remember all the way which Yahweh your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness

parts.title: Part Two · Hear, Israel
parts.epigraph: You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.

parts.title: Part Three · An Open Hand
parts.epigraph: you shall surely open your hand to him

parts.title: Part Four · Choose Life
parts.epigraph: Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants

paintings.title: long enough
paintings.poem:
some places are holy
and still not home.

they had camped
at the foot of the mountain
where God spoke,

and it would have been easy
to stay.

but the voice
that met them there
said: turn.
take your journey.

the mountain was where
he gave the word.

the road was where
they would learn to live it.

paintings.title: carried
paintings.poem:
you remember
the long walk.

the heat,
the complaining,
the nights you didn't think
you'd make it.

Moses remembers
something else:

a father
with a tired child
up on his shoulders,

all the way
you went,
until you came
to this place.

paintings.title: you have lacked nothing
paintings.poem:
not nothing
to want.

there were forty years
of wanting.

but nothing
to lack.

he knew your walking,
every mile of it,

and every morning
there was enough.

paintings.title: that is enough
paintings.poem:
Moses begged.

just to cross,
just to stand
in the good land
he'd walked toward
for forty years.

and God said:
enough.
speak no more of this.

but he didn't send him away
empty.

go up, he said.
lift up your eyes.
look west, north, south, east.

sometimes the answer is no,
and it comes
with a view.

paintings.title: so near
paintings.poem:
other nations
had tall gods
far away

on mountaintops,
in temples
you could only enter
if you were someone.

Israel had
a God who could be reached
by calling.

no climbing.
no appointment.

just your voice,
whenever.

paintings.title: what your eyes saw
paintings.poem:
memory
is a leaky jar.

what your eyes saw,
the fire, the voice,
the bread on the ground,

drips out
a little every day
if you leave it
standing.

so pour it out
on purpose:

tell your children.
tell their children.

a story told
is a story kept.

paintings.title: with all your heart
paintings.poem:
even from far away.
even from the place
you ended up
because you wandered.

from there,
Moses says,
you shall seek.

and from there
you shall find.

he is a merciful God.
he doesn't forget
what he promised

just because
you did.

paintings.title: alive today
paintings.poem:
most of the people listening
had been children at Sinai,
or not yet born.

and Moses says:
not with our fathers.
with us.

the promise
isn't a family heirloom
in a box.

it is spoken
to whoever is standing here,
alive,
today.

that includes you.

paintings.title: hear
paintings.poem:
before any rule,
a word:

hear.

not do.
not try harder.

just stop
and listen.

one God.

so one love,
not divided:

all your heart,
all your soul,
all your strength,

given to the one
who gave it all
to you.

paintings.title: the doorpost
paintings.poem:
not in a temple.
at the door.

where you come in tired.
where you go out
to work.

where the kids run through
a hundred times a day.

talk about them, he says,
when you sit,
when you walk,
when you lie down,
when you get up.

faith isn't a room
in the house.

it's the doorway
to all of them.

paintings.title: when your son asks
paintings.poem:
he won't ask
for a lecture.

he'll ask
what all this means.

so don't start
with rules.

start with:
we were slaves.

and then tell him
about the hand
that brought us out.

paintings.title: the fewest
paintings.poem:
he didn't choose them
because they were many.

they were the fewest.

he didn't choose them
because they were impressive.

he chose them
because he loves.

that's the whole reason.

it was never
about the size of the flower.

paintings.title: not by bread alone
paintings.poem:
he let them
be hungry.

then fed them
with bread
no one had ever seen,

bread you couldn't store
or earn,

only gather,
each morning,
and trust.

you are fed
by the one who speaks,

not by what you can
keep in a jar.

paintings.title: a good land
paintings.poem:
after forty years
of sand,

Moses reads them the list
like a menu:

brooks and springs,
wheat and barley,
vines and figs,
pomegranates,
olives and honey.

you shall eat
and be full,

and then,
he says,

bless him.

paintings.title: when you are full
paintings.poem:
the wilderness
wasn't the dangerous part.

hunger kept them
looking up.

the danger
was coming later:

the fine house,
the growing flocks,
the silver,
the full plate,

and a heart
slowly lifted up
until it forgets
whose hand
brought it out.

remember in the plenty
what you learned
in the sand.

paintings.title: the heart's foreskin
paintings.poem:
the sign on the body
was never meant
to stop at the body.

God wanted
the covering
cut away
from the heart,

the hard layer,
the stiff neck,
the part that won't
turn when he calls.

he wasn't asking for less of you.

he was asking
for the real you,
uncovered.

paintings.title: the foreigner
paintings.poem:
the great God,
the mighty,
the awesome,

who takes
no bribes,

spends his time
on the fatherless,
the widow,
and the stranger
who needs bread
and a coat.

so love the stranger.

you know
how it feels.

you were one.

paintings.title: the rain of the sky
paintings.poem:
Egypt had a river.
you watered your field
with your foot,
turning the channels.

the new land
had hills,
and drank
from the sky.

which meant
you'd have to trust.

but it also meant
someone was watching it,

from the first day of the year
to the last,

every hillside,
every valley.

paintings.title: the tithe feast
paintings.poem:
you'd expect
the tithe
to be taken away.

instead God says:
bring it
and eat it,
in front of me.

road too long?
carry silver instead,
and buy what you like
when you get there.

then sit down,
all of you,
and rejoice.

the offering
was a feast
he was throwing
for you.

paintings.title: open your hand
paintings.poem:
a closed hand
and a hard heart

usually come together.

so do
an open hand
and a heart
that isn't grieved
when it gives.

the poor, Moses says,
won't disappear.

so don't wait
for the problem
to be solved.

open your hand
today.

paintings.title: not empty
paintings.poem:
it wasn't enough
to open the door.

when the servant
walked out free,

you were to fill his arms:
grain from the floor,
wine from the press,
something from the flock.

why?

because you remember
the morning
you walked out of Egypt

and did not
leave with nothing.

paintings.title: altogether joyful
paintings.poem:
seven days
under branches.

after the grain
and the grapes
were in.

and the guest list
went all the way down:

son, daughter,
servants,
the Levite,
the stranger,
the orphan,
the widow.

no one
was supposed to celebrate
alone.

paintings.title: you may not hide yourself
paintings.poem:
it's easy
not to see
a wandering sheep.

it isn't yours.
you're busy.

but the law
says: see it.

bring it back.
and if you don't know
whose it is,

take it home,
feed it,
keep it
until someone
comes looking.

love
is not looking away.

paintings.title: the mother bird
paintings.poem:
a nest by the road,
a mother on her eggs.

and even here,
in a small thing,
the law says:
let her go.

God noticed
the bird.

he wanted you
to notice her too.

paintings.title: the forgotten sheaf
paintings.poem:
you missed one.

don't go back.

leave the olives
on the high branch.
leave the grapes
you didn't get to.

someone is coming
behind you
with an empty basket.

what you forget
is how God
remembers them.

paintings.title: the basket
paintings.poem:
you set the basket down
and tell the story,
out loud:

my father was a wanderer,
ready to perish.

we went down to Egypt
few in number.

we were slaves.
we cried out.
he heard.

he brought us here.

and here
is the first
of what the ground gave.

every basket
is a small testimony.

paintings.title: sandals
paintings.poem:
forty years
of stones and sand

and your sandals
did not wear out.

no one writes songs
about sandals.

but think of every step
they carried,
every morning
they held.

the miracles
you walk in
are the easiest
to miss.

paintings.title: the secret things
paintings.poem:
some things
he keeps.

the why.
the when.
what's around the corner.

and some things
he hands you,
open,
plain as daylight.

don't spend your life
at the locked box.

live
by the lamp.

paintings.title: very near
paintings.poem:
no one needs to climb
to heaven for it.

no one needs to sail
across the sea.

it isn't too hard.
it isn't too far.

it's already here,
in your mouth,
in your heart.

close enough
to do.

paintings.title: choose
paintings.poem:
two roads,
laid out plain.

God doesn't hide
which one he wants.

choose life.

and then he tells you
what life is:

to love him,
to hear him,
to cling to him.

for he is
your life,

and the length
of your days.

paintings.title: he goes before you
paintings.poem:
Moses wasn't going.

so he called Joshua
in front of everyone
and said:

be strong.
be courageous.

not because
you are.

because the Lord
is already
on the other side
of the river,

going ahead,
not leaving,
not letting go.

paintings.title: like rain
paintings.poem:
he didn't want to pound it in.

he wanted his words
to fall
like rain

on new grass,
like dew
you don't hear arrive

but find in the morning
all over everything.

paintings.title: the eagle
paintings.poem:
he found them
in a howling waste

and kept them
as the apple of his eye.

and then,
like an eagle,

he stirred up the nest.

it felt like
falling.

but the wings
were already underneath,

spread wide,

and they were carried
on his feathers
the whole way home.

paintings.title: underneath
paintings.poem:
above
is the sky
he rides on to help you.

around
is the home
you live in, which is him.

and when you can't hold on,

underneath:
arms
that don't get tired.

paintings.title: Nebo
paintings.poem:
he climbed up
from the plains,

and God
showed him everything:

Gilead to Dan,
Judah to the sea,
the palms of Jericho.

you shall see it,
God said,
with your eyes.

and Moses looked
the way you look
at a promise
you know
will be kept.

paintings.title: no one knows where
paintings.poem:
a hundred and twenty years,
his eyes still clear.

and he died
according to the word,
there in Moab.

and it seems God himself
buried him.

no stone.
no shrine.
no place to go and stand.

only the words
he left behind,

and the people
walking on without him,

toward the land
he'd seen.
